targets.approach: Use the Arrowhead Peak approach, but do not go as far into the bowl. Drive to the Fairy Lake road, pass the Shafthouse trailhead, and park beyond the Forest Service gate beside the two well-used campsites. Pick up the narrow trail opposite the parking area, cross the creek and climb the short steep hill to the big meadow, then follow the trail nearly to the top of it, stopping short of the line of trees at the saddle. Leave the trail to the left and go through a gap in the small ridge; Arrowhead is the tallest peak in the bowl, behind the gray limestone wall. Go up the loose scree apron to the right as far as the first big gully. This is among the lowest crack systems on the east face; it begins at a broken crack set a little up from the arete, at the downhill end of the limestone wall.
targets.descent_text: Above the second pitch, a walk east leads to the scree gully that lies straight above the start; descend it to the packs.
targets.name: My ex girlfriend is in love with a road biker

targets.approach: From the sign at Ross Pass, angle left of the Shish Kabob summit to where the terrain forms a gully. There is no defined trail, so follow the path of least resistance down the gully. Routes lie on both sides of it, and Run Ross Run is on skier's left, across from Red October.
targets.name: Run Ross Run

targets.approach: Take the usual No Sweat approach trail to the point beneath the ramp that gives access to the Awakening Wall and the routes on the upper rim, then work westward along faint game trails to the Gray and Pro wall area, and traverse beneath the wall to a big arete on the right of a massive rocky gully. A bolt on this arete marks the start of the first pitch.
targets.descent_text: All the anchors are bolted and set up for rappelling, so the route is descended by rappelling it.
targets.name: Amnesia

targets.approach: From the Beehive Basin trailhead hike up the basin to the lake. Honey Bee Wall is the obvious rock formation on the northwest side of the lake. The route is the most obvious crack on the left side of the wall.
targets.name: Honey Bee

targets.approach: From the Beehive Basin trailhead hike up the basin to the lake. Honey Bee Wall is the obvious rock formation on the northwest side of the lake. The route starts below the discontinuous crack on the right side of the wall, where a rightward-slanting ledge at the lower left gives access to the crack.
targets.name: Prairie Chicken

targets.approach: Log Jam Boulder is on the east side of the lake near the logs in the water, a short way south of the lake campsites. It is the largest boulder in the talus pile, and the route is on its lake-facing side.
targets.name: Otter's Paw

targets.approach: Log Jam Boulder is on the east side of the lake near the logs in the water, a short way south of the lake campsites. It is the largest boulder in the talus pile, and the route is on its lake-facing side.
targets.name: Vampire Seduction

targets.approach: Follow the Lost Cabin Lake Trail until just short of the lake, then climb the talus up to the base of the buttress. The line begins to the right of the big arete's foot and mostly stays on the crest.
targets.name: Lost Cabin Lake Arete

targets.approach: Take the trail toward Lost Cabin Lake and leave it just short of the lake. Go up talus to the right of the trail to the obvious gray slab on the buttress, northwest of the lake.
targets.descent_text: The route finishes on top of the buttress crest. The back of the formation is a walk-off that rejoins the trail.
targets.name: Lost Cabin Lake Buttress - Gray Slab arete

targets.approach: Start at the East Rosebud trailhead near Alpine and follow the trail south beyond the head of the lake, passing a rock outcrop, a stream ford, a large waterfall and a run of switchbacks. Leave the trail where a wide talus wash climbs toward the left flank of the Lower Doublet, and follow the wash through chockstones and boulders until a cliff band has been passed on the right and a vertical waterfall appears. Go right there, up a fourth-class slab, to the hillside directly below the Lower Doublet. The line takes the central prow of the Lower Doublet.
targets.descent_text: The descent is by rappel down the route.
targets.name: Montana Hardman Route

targets.approach: Approach from Beehive Basin or the North Fork trailhead. The formation is an obvious prow at the end of the ridge dividing Bear and Middle basins. Go from the trail to the base through the talus, staying on the trail until some elevation has been gained rather than cutting up early. From the base keep heading south to the foot of a short lead with a clear corner crack and a two-bolt anchor visible above.
targets.descent_text: Walk off to the northeast. If a rappel is needed, it goes straight down.
targets.name: Intraocular hot sauce

targets.approach: From the Granite Lake trailhead hike to the southern end of the lake and circle it to the far end, where a peninsula has a primitive campsite. Stay to climber's right of the feature called Thunderdome and follow the obvious gully and snow slope. Look for a big block that has partly pulled away from the wall, with a ramp running up on its right; the route starts at the crack where the block meets the cliff, or up the ramp.
targets.name: The Stumbling Stone

targets.approach: Park west of Logan Pass, then cross the basin beneath the road to the foot of the slab. Climb the talus cone that rises to the slab, keeping to its left flank. The line is a broken crack system on clean rock straight above a big boulder, which doubles as the first belay stance.
targets.descent_text: From the top walk up a little, then traverse hard left back to the Oberlin climbers trail, which leads to the parking lot.
targets.name: Tee Time

targets.approach: Take the North Rim approach in Mill Creek, and once beyond the Pirate's Cove sector keep going up canyon below the cliff. This is the Upper Tier, and the White Wall is part of it. Kids with Guns opens the White Wall, reached where the path steepens past Pirate's Cove; look for a large pine toward the top of the wall and a line of bolts trending right up through the chossy roof feature.
targets.descent_text: All anchors are bolted, so the route can be rappelled, or you can walk off toward the Tick Farm area.
targets.name: Kids with Guns
